articles.title: GTA 6: Novo trailer de gameplay tem mais de 25 minutos | G1
articles.standfirst: Game mais aguardado do ano vai ser lançado em 19 de novembro. Prévia está disponível para assinantes Netflix, mas fica disponível no YouTube às 22h.
articles.summary: Com lançamento em 19 de novembro, GTA 6 revela 25 minutos de gameplay com os protagonistas Lucia e Jason em trailer disponível na Netflix e no YouTube.
articles.body:
Cena do primeiro trailer de 'GTA 6' — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube/Rockstar Games

"Grand Theft Auto 6" ganhou um novo trailer com "olhar estendido" nesta quinta-feira (27).

A longa prévia, de mais de 25 minutos, está disponível para assinantes da Netflix de forma exclusiva até 22h, quando chega ao canal da desenvolvedora Rockstar no YouTube.

O serviço de streaming chegou a apresentar instabilidade no momento do lançamento, segundo o site Down Detector.

O vídeo começa com o casal de protagonistas, Lucia e Jason, metido em um tiroteio entre uma gangue de traficantes de drogas e a polícia em um prédio, e mostra momentos de gameplay da ação — ou seja, sequências que poderão ser controladas pelos jogadores.

Também há um vislumbre de como funciona a mecânica da troca dos comandos sobre os dois. Em um momento, enquanto ele dirige um carro em fuga pela polícia, o jogador passa de forma instantânea a controlá-la e atira nas autoridades.

Em outro, a prévia dá a entender que é possível fazer a transição mesmo com os dois personagens bem longe um do outro.

Game mais aguardado do ano, "GTA 6", como o jogo de ação em mundo aberto é conhecido, vai ser lançado para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X e S em 19 de novembro.

articles.title: I Turned a Skeleton Into a Roast Chicken in Fable, and I’d Do It Again | gamescom 2026
articles.summary: We finally played Fable, and there's a surprising amount of depth to be found in its spell-slinging combat. Our hands-on preview:
articles.body:
Yesterday I got to see a full quest from Fable being played live . That demo largely focussed on the city of Bowerstone, the characters in the capital, and the choices that can be made within each mission. While there were a couple of flashes of combat within what I saw, I wanted to reserve judgment on the action until I got hands on with Fable myself. Well, now I have, and I’m pleasantly surprised by what I played. While there’s joy to be found in the devastating thud of a giant hammer, what impressed me the most is how each of its varied magic spells work in harmony with the foundational melee systems. And that’s all before we get to the chickens. It wouldn’t be Fable without chickens, after all.

Although story, world, and characters power a lot of Fable’s charm and will remain just as significant to Playground’s reimagining as they were in the original series, there will be no escaping the rigors of combat here. You’re a hero, after all, and no matter how good you are at talking your way out of sticky situations, you’ll need to get your hands dirty regularly.

“Heroes are sort of humans plus plus, right?” Fable’s game director, Ralph Fulton, tells me. “They're special, stronger, more charismatic, all that kind of stuff. So combat, and obviously the ability to wield control and wield magic is another thing that sets you apart from the regulars. Combat feels like the place where you're going to show your differences most effectively. The golden line will have combat throughout it. I wouldn't say absolutely every quest features a combat beat, although I would say most do.”

When it’s time to get stuck in, Fable doesn’t want to limit your combat options. Unlike more rigid RPGs, there’s no class system to lock into, nor any other species or job parameters that dictate what sort of experience you can have. Instead, you’re encouraged to experiment with all options in pursuit of a loadout of magic abilities that complement your chosen playstyle. To showcase how this works and redefines the experience, I got to play through a mid-game mission called Mud and Death twice. Both times I was equipped with the same massive two-handed hammer and ranged bow, but the selected spells were different on each run: One included, a lightning strike, fireball, animal-transformation, and stealth-shift move behind an enemy’s back in its spellbook, whereas the other had the same lightning strike, a levitation spell that can turn into a ground pound, magical blades that hover before attacking multiple targets, and force push-esque magical shove (in the full game you’ll be able to switch in and out your loadout of spells and weapons on the fly, but for the purposes of this demo it was locked in for me.)

The mission itself was simple, but provided me with plenty of enemy fodder to play around with. Reanimated skeletons stumbled towards me, Ray Harryhausen-style, with the aim of sinking their swords into me. Although they initially seemed a simplistic foe to be unthinkingly batted away, plenty of interesting touches emerged from each I fought, such as how some produce a wailing wraith from their crumpled bones upon striking them down. The most fun thing to play around with, however, is how these undead react to the damage you inflict on them. For example, send an arrow into their knee, and they’ll fall down and start crawling along the ground toward you. Manage to knock their skulls from their spine? They’ll lose the ability to aim and end up firing their crossbow bolts in all sorts of directions.

Lopping off those heads feels great, too. Sharpshooting with a fully drawn longbow is accompanied by a satisfying “ping”, and while rattling a full magazine of repeating crossbow ammunition into exposed cheekbone didn’t give me quite as much gratification, it by no means felt bad. By far the best mode of undead beheading that I got to try out though was swinging that big hammer in a calcium-enriched game of croquet. Both light and heavy attacks are available, and if you hold in their respective buttons, you’ll get charged up versions. I particularly enjoyed the hammer’s charged heavy option, which proved great for crowd control as my hero spun around several times, knocking down anything in their path.

It’s worth noting just how many waves of enemies I faced during these encounters. I initially wondered if this was purely for demo purposes to allow for the breadth of combat options to be shown off completely, but later confirmed with Playground that this is genuinely the number of foes that will appear during this mission in the final game. Anyone who has played Lionhead’s Fable games will recognise this approach, and Playground sees this as a continuation of the original trilogy’s ability to make each encounter feel like a heroic event.

“What the original Fable games did, which was often putting you in one-to-many combat scenarios, felt like that was a great way of shining a light on your capital H heroism,” Fulton explains. “Rather than it being sort of an equal duel, oftentimes it's you against a bunch of enemies. And that seems like a forum for you to be able to go and express yourself and feel like a hero because that's ultimately the fantasy of the game.”

The traditional weaponry feels good with its modern action game approach of dodging, blocking, a parrying incorportated, but it’s when slinging those spells that Fable’s combat fully came alive for me. Across my two playthroughs I accessed sorcery ranging from levitating multiple enemies into the air and sending them crashing back down to the floor, summon lightning strikes down upon them, and unleash fireballs. There’s some great synergy to be found in combining spells and attacks; for example, I could lift a bunch of skeletons into the air, but before sending them down to the ground, I could hit them with the lightning spell which made their brittle bones burst into pieces in middair.

By far the best combination, though, involved a series staple creature.

It just wouldn’t be Fable without chickens. The Befowl spell lets you turn an enemy into a little clucker, and when fully upgraded, will allow you to multiply that effect onto others. But lend this fate to a skeleton warrior, and you won’t just get any chicken. You’ll get an undead chicken trotting around the place, glowing green and looking far from tasty. That can changed, though. Send a fireball in its direction and they’ll transform into a freshly roasted chicken, ending them as a threat completely. It’s these sort of experimental actions – and the comedic results that can be conjured from them – that make me most excited about the possibilities Fable’s suite of spells could lead to.

“We knew we were going to get humor in lots of areas of the game and the big question mark was, ‘Is combat meant to be funny? Should it be funny or should it be an inherently serious pursuit?’ says Fulton. “As it's turned out, and again, game development's often like this, we've found the funny in combat down the line. The chicken spell is funny in and of itself, but the team really ran with it, which I love.”

Some enemies are, sadly, resistant to such foolishness. My demo ended with a boss fight set in the confines of the foggy Wraithmarsh. Waiting for me there was an entity called the Lantern Keeper, essentially a twisted mesh of twigs with branches for limbs and a glowing green lamp for a head. Its beefy health bar posed a challenge, and while its dry and woody frame wasn’t a fan of my searing fireball spell, I couldn’t repeatedly target it with flame due to a relatively restrictive cooldown placed on each incantation. That’s where my bow came in handy, and firing arrow after arrow into its head proved a very viable tactic — turns out having your weak point light up and stick out like a sore thumb through thick mist isn’t the smartest idea.

That didn’t mean it was a simple fight, though. The Lantern Keeper has a few big attacks up their sleeve, as well as the ability to spawn wraiths. Though annoying in numbers, these spectral mobs are easy to take down, and at times it became vital that I did so. Let the boss deal big damage to you, and you’ll naturally find yourself in need of a health boost. The only way to refill your potions, though, is by collecting green orbs that fall from enemies once you’ve killed them – a system that pays homage to the original games without directly cloning. I love this approach to action in games, as it encourages you to play on the front foot, and while Fable’s version is nowhere near as fast or as well-oiled a machine as the systems the power the likes of Doom Eternal or Control Resonant, I’m always a fan of attack being the best form of defense.

The action is promised to develop over the course of the main quest, too, with both complexity in boss design and new ways to take them down introduced throughout. “There are a couple of skills that you can acquire. One is called Return to Sender, which is where you can sort of grab projectiles out the air and return them,” reveals Fulton. “You can do that to a lot of magical spells as well. So some of the boss fights that you will encounter later in the game almost become sort of like this trading. Any spell that you cast is probably coming back at you and vice versa. So they become much more tactical at that point.”

My overall takeway from finally playing Fable for myself was that the fluidity of its combat systems feels great to wield, and, I promise you, as is often the case, better than just watching it. There’s a great sense of flexibility in the tools at your disposal and how best to combo them to create chain effects and increased damage. The more standard side of combat — dodging, blocking and parrying with a physical weapon — is smooth if not groundbreaking. But throw those stylish spells into the mix, and you’ve got a fantastic translation of the original Fable’s combat into the modern age. Just don’t try eating the zombie chickens.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Fable Was Previously Aiming for an October Launch, Director Reveals, Insisting That the Game's Delay Wasn't Due to Being 'Scared of Other Big Games'
articles.summary: Fable is set to release on February 23, 2027, and developer Playground Games is feeling pretty confident that it will be ready for that date.
articles.body:
Fable is set to release on February 23, 2027, and developer Playground Games is feeling pretty confident that it will be ready for that date.

Speaking to IGN at gamescom, the RPG’s director, Ralph Fulton, told us that he feels “great about it.”

“I think the rationale behind moving us out of October, the date that we were in previously, is pretty apparent to everybody,” he continues. “I feel great about that. I mean, I was really looking forward to shipping this game this year. I didn't want to have to do another January 1st speech to the team about ‘this is the year we ship Fable,’ which I'm now going to have to do. But the rationale for it is absolutely sound. I'm glad that we're avoiding that chaotic window.”

This is actually the first we’ve officially heard about the game having previously been earmarked for an October 2026. Prior to the announcement of the February date, we had only been given a window of "this fall.”

It makes sense that Playground’s reimagining of the formerly Microsoft-exclusive series decided to move out of October. Fulton isn’t wrong about it being a chaotic time of year with another Xbox Games Studio release, Gears of War E-Day coming that month, along with the likes of PS5 console exclusive, Phantom Blade Zero.

Those games are sandwiched between a packed September involving the likes of Marvel’s Wolverine, Control Resonant, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Silent Hill: Townfall to name but a few. That doesn’t mean February of next year is looking any clearer, though, with many other game developers seemingly having had a similar idea to Fable. Indeed, Playground's RPG will launch against God of War Laufey, Metro 2039, and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

Fulton isn’t worried about the beginning of next year suddenly looking like another busy period for big games releases, however. “People keep saying that to me, but we don't run scared of other big games,” says Fulton.

“We're a big game ourselves. We hold ourselves to high standards. I'm happy to go toe-to-toe with a bunch of other games. There's just one that I'm happy to avoid entirely.”

That game is, of course, GTA 6. Stay tuned tonight for more on Rockstar’s upcoming return to Vice City, where we’ll have plenty of reaction and insight alongside the Extended Look debuting on Netflix.

For more Fable, check out our gamescom previews where we’ve got impressions of a full quest , plus our thoughts on how its combat is shaping up after playing.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Alien Deathstorm: How the Aliens Vs Predator Games Influenced the Survival Horror | gamescom 2026 - IGN

articles.title: Toy Story 5 Is Coming to Disney+ Next Month
articles.summary: Toy Story 5, which is now the highest-grossing movie in the franchise, is officially coming to Disney+ on September 23.
articles.body:
Toy Story 5 is officially coming to Disney+ on September 23.

The streaming release date is just over four months after the film’s initial release in theaters, a standard timeline for Pixar movies. A spread of 4K Blu-rays, including a highly sought after 4K steelbook , will be released the day before, on September 22. The movie is also already available to rent or purchase digitally from PVOD platforms.

A new trailer was released in anticipation of the Disney+ arrival that largely features an army of Buzz Lightyears. The streaming release announcement is also accompanied by a new music video for the piano version of the Taylor Swift song featured in the movie, “I Knew It, I Knew You," now available on Spotify, Apple Music, and Disney+.

Toy Story 5 grossed just over $1.1 billion worldwide with a reported budget of $250 million, surpassing the box office performance of the previous sequel, Toy Story 4 . The Toy Story franchise as a whole has now grossed over $3.3 billion, and only slightly trails behind Universal's Despicable Me as the second highest-grossing animated media franchise of all time.

The latest Pixar sequel introduces a new villain, LilyPad, tackling the topic of technology for kids . Following the end of Toy Story 4, Woody is a little less of a main character , with the movie instead focusing more on Jessie, Buzz, and a gaggle of new characters.

The movie currently sits at a 93% rating on Rotten Tomatoes , the lowest in the very acclaimed franchise . Critic Clint Gage gave the film a 7/10 in his review for IGN , saying it ultimately "manages to pull off an adventurous and resonant conclusion."

The sequel's box office success follows what Pixar reported as a disappointing run for Hoppers, which was in part blamed for recent layoffs at the studio . Still, Pixar will be going back to originals with its next movie, Gatto , slated for release next March. There’s been no official word on what’s next for the Toy Story saga, but the franchise does seem to always find its way back .

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Elden Ring Update Patch Notes Reveal Biggest Changes in Years
articles.summary: FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years.
articles.body:
FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years.

The developer caught fans off-guard with lengthy patch notes today, detailing a list of buffs (and a few nerfs) for different weapons and playstyles across the game. It's a major update that arrived as FromSoftware prepares for the launch of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Nintendo Switch 2, as well as its accompanying DLC for other platforms.

What we have here is a laundry list of balance adjustments that get under the hood to tweak a variety of PvE and PvP tools. Based on the list of updates available on the Dark Souls developer's website , the last time we received patch notes of a similar length was back in October 2024, a few months after the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion released. That makes it not only one of the biggest updates the 2022 game-of-the-year winner has received in years, but what could be one of its final ones, too.

Generally, what Elden Ring players have to look forward to is a lot of buffs. The Firespark, Lightning, Chilling, Frenzyflame, and Deadly Poison Perfume Bottles, for example, got increased attack power across the board. The Smithscript Axe and Spear, as well as the Spear of the Impaler, also benefit from reduced stamina use and increased power for thrown attacks.

The August Elden Ring update also comes with increased guard boost and reduced weight for the Lordsworn's Shield, Briar Greatshield, Spiked Palisade Shield, and more. Others, such as the Wooden Greatshield, Cuckoo Greatshield, Redmane Greatshield, and Crucible Hornshield, also got increased guard boost.

Another big change hits everyone's favorite FromSoftware mechanic: parries. You'll now notice improved parry performance across the board, for example, with the developer also explaining it's reduced the time before certain actions can be performed when using things like Daggers, Curved Swords, and Small Shields post-parry.

The nerfs, meanwhile, hit the Gravitational Missile and Great Katana. The former has been altered so that its projectile will not explode upon impact with terrain, while the latter now suffers from increased damage when hit by other players during an attack. The update also squashed bugs related to the Great Katana weapon, as well as a few PC-exclusive glitches.

For a game that turned four years old back in February, Elden Ring is still going strong. How much juice is left in the tank remains to be seen, though, as FromSoftware is very much staying busy with other projects . The Duskbloods , for example, may be a Switch 2 exclusive , but judging by the reactions to its first network test , it could compete with the studio's other multiplayer experiences.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition will keep the train rolling when it launches tomorrow, August 28, for Switch 2 owners, with all of today's updates in tow. The Tarnished Pack DLC – which includes the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight starting classes, three Torrent skins, and four new armor sets – will also release for other platforms tomorrow.

Today's update is out now for players across PC, PlayStation 4, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. You can check out the full patch notes below. For more, you can read about the Elden Ring movie , which wrapped filming in July . You can also learn about the social media post that had fans hoping to return to the Lands Between for even more content.

articles.title: Heads Up: GTA 6 Preloads Begin November 12
articles.summary: If you're already plotting how to ditch work for a week in November to play GTA 6, you'll want to make sure to preload the game on your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. Here's when you'll be able to.
articles.body:
I know a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6-related news is dropping today, but I wanted to remind/tell you about what to expect if you preorder. Preorders are live now , and the game will be released on November 19. But if you preorder, you’ll be able to download a copy onto your PS5 or Xbox Series S|X starting November 12 , according to Rockstar . That way you’ll be able to start playing the moment it’s released.

Grand Theft Auto 6 (Physical - Code in a Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition (Digital)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - PS5 Physical (Code in Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Xbox Physical (Code in Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition Upgrade

That preload date works for both digital and “physical” preorders. I put the word physical in scare quotes because, while you do get a physical box, it doesn’t include a disc. Physical copies of GTA 6 are a code in a box. But that box will ship to you on November 12, at which point you can enter the code into your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S to download the game.

If you haven’t already preordered GTA 6 and you want to take advantage of the early preload situation, you’ll have to decide whether to buy it in digital or physical format . You’ll also have to decide whether you want the $79.99 standard edition or the $99.99 ultimate edition, the latter of which it turns out most people are preordering . Note that there’s no physical version of the ultimate edition, but you can buy the “Ultimate Edition Upgrade” for $20 on the PlayStation Store or Xbox Store.

All preorders come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+. Note that the GTA+ subscription auto-renews, so you’ll want to go ahead and set a reminder to cancel if you don’t want to continue paying for it. Here’s what’s in the Vintage Vice City Pack:

'55 VAPID STANIER: Cruise Shore Drive in this classic sedan and store it just a stone's throw from the glistening sands of Ocean Beach in the Shore Court garage, complete with a weapon locker plus a secure place to deposit stolen goods to be fenced.

OUTFITS AND HAIRSTYLES: Dress for excess with Jason’s effortlessly chic linen suit in vintage pastel, complemented by the cut and coif of the decade of decadence. Show everyone the world is yours in Lucia’s red sequin mini dress and curls.

EXCLUSIVE WEAPON PATTERN: Adorn most guns with a tropical pattern inspired by Tommy Vercetti's iconic palm tree button-up.

The Vintage Vice City Pack is included with all digital purchases of Grand Theft Auto VI made prior to November 20, 2026.

The ultimate edition includes the base game, plus a ton of extra digital content that Rockstar says is “threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia’s story.” Here’s what’s included:

’95 GROTTI CHEETAH: Grotti's signature mid '90s sports car and ode to Shore Drive, the ’95 Grotti Cheetah is complete with a minimalist, retro-futuristic livery and available to punctuate later-stage action.

HAWK & LITTLE MORGAN REVOLVER: His and hers versions of this powerful revolver with classic Vice City stylings sourced from the Vercetti Estate, including palm-tree-etched grips, engraved detailing, and high-performance scope.

PERSONALIZED WEAPON VARIANTS: Personalized sidearms with detailed engravings for Jason's Girardi ES9 pistol and Lucia's Klose K17 pistol.

VICE CITY STYLE: Whether poolside or side by side, Jason and Lucia can look the part with exclusive outfits, hairstyles, tattoos, and more.

JASON’S SAFEHOUSE VEHICLES: Switch gears and soak up the sun in an Army fatigue-tinged Dinka Enduro motorcycle or Crest Kayak.

GANADO RETRO BUILD: Inject some muscle and classic stylings into Jason's well-worn Vapid Ganado low-riding pickup with exclusive mods.

SHITZU SQUALO: Perfect for casting in Gambit Bay and reeling in catches of all sorts, this gradient pink and blue Squalo docked at Washington Beach is made open-ocean-ready with an explosives-laden weapons crate.

'67 VAPID DOMINATOR BUGGY & GARAGE: A Mud Club monster offering impressive off-road handling for the backwoods of Mount Kalaga and beyond. Conveniently store it at the Paradise Garage in Watson Bay, which features a weapon locker plus a secure place to deposit stolen goods to be fenced.

GOODTIME GEAR: A capsule collection of apparel and accessories inspired by the Goodtime State’s hit TV show character, Macca the Alligator.

PTT YOUNGIN$ COMPOUND: Raid the compound of one of Southside Vice City’s loudest and most socially active gangs and escape safely to score some special items and distinct contraband.

CLASSIC CAR COLLECTION: Track down a variety of abandoned classic and work-in-progress project cars and revitalize them to their former glory in this special commission from eccentric collector and local fixer, Wyman.

Special Destinations Only Open for Business with the Ultimate Edition:

RIDEOUT CUSTOMS: Transform vanilla vehicles into magnificent works of art with detailed interiors, exquisite rims, and donk stylings.

SARA'S UNISEX SALON: Get signature salon styles for both Jason and Lucia, including facial hair for Jason and makeup and nails for Lucia.

STOCK 305: Style various unique and exclusive looks for Jason and Lucia at Stockyard’s premiere destination for elevated streetwear.

ELECTRIC FANG TATTOO: Choose from over 50 signature tattoos for both Jason and Lucia — all designed by the artist collective FAILE at Stockyard’s most iconic ink bar.

ONE-EYED WILLIE’S: Visit Lake Leonida’s storied mod shop, specializing in off-road modifications and hand-painted automotive artistry.

Now it's time to schedule vacation from work to coincide with the November 19 launch... For full preorder info, check out our official Grand Theft Auto 6 Preorder Guide , which has everything you need to know, and a whole lot more.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: The Way You Steal Cars in GTA 6 Completely Changes the Game
articles.summary: Stealing cars is no longer a case of just tapping a button in GTA 6. Rockstar reveals how it has added “layers of stratification” to make the theft in Grand Theft Auto a little more challenging.
articles.body:
Ever since the first game launched back in 1997, Grand Theft Auto’s titular crime has been a fairly simple process: tap one button and someone else’s car is now yours. Almost 30 years later, GTA 6 is set to change that completely, introducing a tiered vehicle security system, a varied set of tools to steal them with, and new ways to profit from each theft directly. Let’s look at the details of how it all works in Rockstar’s latest, as well as theorise about what it could all mean for other styles of robbery, including liquor store hold-ups and big bank heists.

Long-term GTA fans will be more than familiar with how stealing a car has worked in the series thus far. You walk up to your desired wheels and simply press a button to open a door left carelessly unlocked, or smash through the window with your elbow to enter better secured vehicles. That simplicity won’t be going away completely in GTA 6, it appears, with older, less desirable vehicles still vulnerable to swift methods of entry, such as a quick slim jim forced into the window gap and under the lock. But other, much more high-end motors will come packed with added security layers that introduce new gameplay challenges, asking players to flex unfamiliar muscles when it comes to jacking cars.

“We have put some layers of stratification into the vehicles,” explains Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North. “Previously, you could just press triangle to automatically hotwire and steal any vehicle that you wanted and take off. We felt like that left a lot of potential gameplay on the table, in terms of progression and decision-making for players. I think it gives all the vehicles more meaning, and you need to pay attention to what you’re doing a bit more.”

But how will you know which cars will be harder to crack than others? Well, apart from passing a quick eye test of being able to distinguish a rusty old white van from a straight off the production line Grotti sports car, you’ll need to take advantage of a new bit of GTA 6 tech: the WAINK scanner.

Get within range of any vehicle that takes your fancy, and you’ll be able to hold your device up to get all of the relevant information. Chief among these details are its security system and value. We don’t yet know how many car security tiers there’ll be, but what we do know is that some will be protected digitally, as GTA catches up with the modern age of electronic keys. That means you’ll need a digital key cloning device in order to unlock some car doors, but that piece of kit will come at a cost, with it needing to be acquired first. Some tools will only unlock after a certain point in the story, and it’s a clear sign that GTA 6 is aiming to evolve its gameplay opportunities over the course of the game. It’s all in service of adding levels of complexity to binary actions.

But technology can also work against you. Even if you manage to get behind the wheel of your chosen target, that car may be fitted with a tracker — some advanced versions of which reveal your location to law enforcement if you drive below a certain speed, meaning you need to put your foot down to avoid hearing sirens. Not only will it draw police attention your way if the car is reported as stolen, but, in theory, any prospective buyer worth its name in salt would want it removed before you cash in. This ties into another layer of GTA 6’s enhanced simulation – you’ll be able to visit a fence and sell any vehicle you’ve stolen. Yes, Rockstar is borrowing from its previous game, Red Dead Redemption 2, albeit you’ll be hunting metal beasts rather than taking down meaty big bucks for big bucks. And Arthur Morgan never had to worry about GPS trackers ruining the value of his finds.

But perhaps you aren’t stealing a car with pure profit foremost in mind, but instead just fancy making it your own. Well, the WAINK scanner (yes, it’s really called that and I have no idea what that acronym stands for right now) also tells you how much it will cost to register that car as your own. GTA 6 will allow Jason and Lucia to each own multiple personal vehicles, provided you have the cash and garage space.

Both of these new systems — tiered security and fencing — open up a whole new world of possibilities when it comes to mission design in GTA 6. Don’t be surprised to see more organic, emergent solutions to mission objectives appear as you play. For example, the simple fact that many cars can’t be instantly broken into and commandeered makes the act of escape an altogether more frantic endeavor. You might get lucky and slide into an unsecured sedan on the first try, but with the police at your back, you’re realistically not going to have the time to stop and scan the area for the perfect getaway vehicle. It all builds into Rockstar’s intention for you to spend more time scurrying away on foot or changing methods of transport on the fly, with the narrower Leonida streets helping generate exciting desperation and unexpected thrills.

“The streets in this game are narrower, and more realistic in terms of scale”, Nelson explains. “Which, in addition to all the density of the traffic on the roads, makes driving slightly more challenging and requires a bit of skill.”

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

That more organic approach to moment-to-moment action could extend to specific styles of mission, too. Not an insignificant amount of time in both GTA 5 and GTA Online is spent reclaiming cars for Simeon, Franklin’s original employer. These primarily serve as simple, introductory quests to the world of San Andreas and its gameplay fundamentals, but in GTA 6, the framework of similar jobs could become a lot more rewarding with these additional layers of complexity.

Rather than simply placing a marker on your map to drive to and demanding you deliver a predetermined vehicle back to whoever requires it, the possibilities have now opened up, thanks to the WAINK scanner. In theory, you could be asked to find a specific brand of car around the world, or one of a specific value, and use this newfound technology to go on a miniature treasure hunt. Doing so would embed us further into GTA 6’s world and allow us to spend less time following markers and traced lines along roads on a mini map. Being able to take this newly procured car to any fence on the map would also help mix things up, rather than the tedium that zooming along the same few streets back to Simeon’s in Los Santos could become.

But perhaps most exciting is how these systems could translate into GTA 6’s bigger, high-stakes missions. In theory, the back rooms of small stores could be easily broken into, with the minimal spoils waiting there, yours to take. But what about big banks or heavily guarded facilities? Surely some more advanced tech will need to be employed here to crack safes or bypass locked doors. If you don’t have the right tools for the job, such as the aforementioned key cloning device, then does that limit what you’ll take away from a score, or potentially make missions branch in interesting ways? These are all choices that will seemingly add up over the course of GTA 6, and the repercussions could range from short-term problems such as an increased wanted level, to permanently damaging Jason and Lucia’s relationship.

Stealing cars has been at the core of Grand Theft Auto for almost three decades now, but this fundamental change to how it all works is as exciting a change as Rockstar has made in that time. I can’t wait to get my hands on it and see for myself just how much it opens up its world and the possibilities within it.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: GTA VI al detalle: nuevas mecánicas y jugabilidad, HUD al estilo 'Red Dead' y el mapa de Leónida
articles.standfirst: El último metraje de la esperada obra de Rockstar Games revela un sinfín de novedades jugables
articles.summary: El último metraje de la esperada obra de Rockstar Games revela un sinfín de novedades jugables
articles.body: GTA VI: 'Una mirada extendida' nos ha dejado casi media hora de gameplay de la nueva obra de Rockstar, en el que podemos apreciar un montón de detalles de jugabilidad y del nuevo mundo en general que nos ofrece el videojuego más esperado de la historia. El análisis de estas secuencias de juego confirma una profunda evolución en las mecánicas de sigilo, la interacción con el entorno y una notable similitud entre los sistemas de supervivencia e inmersión vistos en Red Dead Redemption 2. Una de las grandes revelaciones se centra en la reestructuración del sistema de búsqueda policial. En plena persecución, los protagonistas pueden despistar a las autoridades adentrándose en aparcamientos y quemando su vehículo de escape mediante un cóctel molotov, lo que provoca la desaparición inmediata del icono del coche en el radar. En el plano jugable, la cooperación entre ambos delincuentes gana en fluidez: el sistema permitirá alternar entre Jason y Lucía en tiempo real con solo pulsar el botón R1, agilizando el ritmo tanto en misiones como en mundo abierto, aunque suponemos que esto estará delimitado en ciertas misiones, en las que tendrás que ir intercambiando con ellos simultáneamente. La interfaz de usuario adopta una clara herencia de las mecánicas de bienestar de Red Dead Redemption 2: - Tres barras de estado: Se incluye una barra de vida con segmento crítico, una barra de energía (stamina) y una nueva barra de cansancio o sueño, lo que apunta a la necesidad de descansar para mantener el rendimiento. - Gestión económica clásica: El HUD vuelve a diferenciar de forma visible en la esquina derecha entre el dinero en efectivo y el saldo disponible en la cuenta bancaria. - Rueda de armas de ocho huecos: Tres ranuras fijas quedan asignadas de inicio para pistola, combate cuerpo a cuerpo (puños) y prismáticos. En el cuadrante inferior izquierdo se integran pastillas y consumibles destinados a recuperar o sobrepotenciar la salud. - Rueda de accesorios y disfraces: Un nuevo menú radial permite equipar o retirar gafas, gorras y máscaras, sumando un icono con forma de percha pensado para cambiar de disfraz o atuendo sobre la marcha. La exposición en redes sociales también tendrá su peso dentro de la experiencia de juego. En una de las secuencias más surrealistas y dinámicas del metraje, Lucía descubre a una suerte de creador de contenido encerrado en el maletero de un vehículo robado, pero lejos de asustarse, el influencer retransmite la persecución policial en riguroso directo, mostrando las reacciones y los comentarios del chat en tiempo real en la esquina superior derecha de la pantalla. A esto se le suma la integración de las aplicaciones de mensajería instantánea, clave para la coordinación en las misiones entre ambos delincuentes. A través del teléfono móvil, los protagonistas se comunican en situaciones límite: el intercambio de mensajes sirve como nexo narrativo entre ambos, y, a través de ellos, es cuando ocurre un cambio inmediato de perspectiva jugable entre los dos. Más allá de los atracos, el metraje ilustra la enorme variedad de actividades que podrás realizar en Leónida. Los jugadores podrán desplazarse en patinete eléctrico, surcar las zonas pantanosas, entrenar con pesas en el gimnasio, jugar al baloncesto en casa, practicar buceo, pilotar motos de agua o competir en circuitos urbanos de velocidad. Una secuencia de salto en paracaídas con Lucía permite contemplar por primera vez, desde una perspectiva cenital y prácticamente en su totalidad, la descomunal escala y densidad geográfica que ofrecerá el mapa de Leónida.
